methods.pose_leg_ms: host: host clock after the apply minus the device capture time mapped through the CLOCK offset
methods.render_readback_ms: host: main-thread draw_view3d of a frame plus its texture read and FrameSlot copy on the next tick (perf_counter), per submitted frame
methods.encode_ms: host: JPEG encode on the native encoder thread (last_sent.encode_ns), sampled once per poll
methods.send_ms: host: VIDEO_FRAGMENT send of all the frame's fragments (last_sent.send_ns), sampled once per poll
methods.network_ms: derived, not timed: the host and device clocks differ, so a fragment's flight time can't be read from either side. At each percentile q, network = M2P(q) - (pose_leg + render_readback + encode + receive + decode + display)(q); send is not subtracted because it overlaps receive. Percentiles don't add, so this is an estimate, clamped at 0 (`clamped` lists where). The residual holds the downlink flight of the first fragment plus the host waits no leg times (apply -> the next render tick, draw -> readback on the following tick, readback -> encoder start), so it is an upper bound on the network time. `crosscheck.clock_one_way_ms` (half the CLOCK round trip, symmetric-path assumption) shows how much of it is flight.
methods.receive_ms: device: tracking queue: first VIDEO_FRAGMENT of a frame read -> its last fragment read (reassembly; the network transit before the first fragment needs the host clock)
methods.decode_ms: device: complete frame handed to the decoder -> ImageIO JPEG decode into the Metal texture done (includes the wait behind a decode in progress)
methods.display_ms: device: texture ready -> display time of the first drawable showing it
methods.m2p_ms: device: display time - capture time of the frame's pose_seq (pose ring on the tracking queue); frames not presented or without a capture time give no sample
methods.display_time: device: MTLCommandBuffer.GPUEndTime (the simulator SDK has no MTLDrawable.presentedTime; excludes the wait for the next display refresh)
methods.device_clock: device: CLOCK_UPTIME_RAW (mach_absolute_time) in ns; ARFrame.timestamp and the Metal display time (CACurrentMediaTime base) are seconds on the same clock, converted by x 1e9 with no offset
methods.percentiles: host legs: nearest rank over every sample; device legs: nearest rank, reported as the upper edge of the histogram bin (0.1 ms for receive/decode/display, 1 ms for M2P), so they never understate

crosscheck.clock_one_way_method: half the round trip delay of the host's newest CLOCK estimate (vcp.md §6.3)
crosscheck.video_report_method: the VIDEO_REPORT.m2p_p95_ms values the host received (each the device's p95 over ~500 ms), summarised by the host

verdict.scope: simulator only: the iPhone simulator on the same Mac as Blender, over loopback. The display time is the command buffer's GPUEndTime (the simulator SDK has no presentedTime), a lower bound that leaves out the wait for the next display refresh. Says nothing about a real iPhone on Wi-Fi.

notes: Blender runs the debug vcam_native wheel tools/mission/setup.sh builds (local release wheels can fail to load, docs/LOOP_LOG.md), so encode_ms and M2P include debug-build JPEG encoding; SRS §13.2 (S-2a) has release encode times near 1 ms at 960x540.
The simulator and Blender share one Mac (CPU, GPU and loopback network); the pose leg and network leg include no Wi-Fi.
needs_owner: M2P and every leg on a real iPhone over 5 GHz Wi-Fi (NFR-LAT-003, NFR-LAT-004)
